nodes.title: Genus-sign reversal
nodes.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Let n ≠ 0 satisfy (4.2): Nn + l ≡ 0 (mod D) for some l = N(𝔞), 𝔞 an integral ideal in A and let d be a positive divisor of n. Then ε_A(n, |n|/d) = −ε(N)·sgn(n)·ε_A(n, d). (Both sides vanish unless (d, n/d, D) = 1. If (d, n/d, D) = 1 write D = D₀D′D″ with D₀, D′, D″ discriminants, |D′| = (d, D), |D″| = (n/d, D), D₀ prime to n; then the product ε_A(n,d)ε_A(n,|n|/d) equals ε_{D₀}(|n|) ε_{D′D″}(−N sgn n) χ_{D₀·D′D″}(A), and (4.2) gives χ_{D₀·D′D″}(A) = ε_{D₀}(l) = ε_{D₀}(−Nn), whence the product is ε_D(−N sgn n) = −ε(N)sgn(n).) In particular, if ε(N) = +1 and n > 0 satisfies (4.2), then Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_A(n,d) = 0.
hypotheses: K=ℚ(√D), D<0 a fundamental discriminant; ε=(D/·), h=#Cl(K), w=#O_K×=2u; A an ideal class; r_A(n) counts integral ideals of norm n and r_A(0)=1/w.

N≥1 is prime to D; f is a weight-2k newform, k≥1, with a(1)=1 where eigenform normalization is used. Petersson pairing is linear in the first argument, with y^(2k)dxdy/y² and no implicit volume division.
proofSteps: Replace d by |n|/d and evaluate the two primitive character signs.
The claimed reversal uses the norm congruence and ε(N); it is not a universal unsigned-divisor identity.

nodes.title: Different ideal reindexing
nodes.statement: With the standing notation (D odd, so D squarefree), for every m ≥ 0 and every class A: r_A(m|D|) = r_A(m). (The different 𝔡 = (√D) is principal and every integral ideal of norm m|D| is divisible by every ramified prime, hence equals 𝔡·𝔟 with N(𝔟) = m; for m = 0 both sides are 1/w.)

(1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). The source genus condition leaves one nonsplit prime; preserve the ramified alternative instead of claiming the same valuation coefficient.

nodes.title: Logarithmic weight-two projection
nodes.statement: Let Φ̃(z) = Σ_{m∈ℤ} a_m(y)e^{2πimx} ∈ M̃₂(Γ₀(N)) satisfy the growth condition (6.1) at all cusps ξ, and suppose A_ξ = A(N₁), B_ξ = B(N₁) depend only on N₁ = gcd(N, denominator of ξ). Let {α(M), β(M) : M | N} be the solution of the non-singular linear system (6.3) Σ_{M|N} ((M,N₁)²/M²) α(M) = A(N₁) (N₁ | N), (6.4) Σ_{M|N} ((M,N₁)²/M²) {β(M) + α(M) log((M,N₁)²/M)} = B(N₁) (N₁ | N). Then there is a holomorphic cusp form Φ = Σ_{m≥1} a_m e^{2πimz} ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) with (Φ, f) = (Φ̃, f) for all f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) and, for (m, N) = 1, (6.5) a_m = lim_{s→0} [4πm ∫₀^∞ a_m(y) e^{−4πmy} y^s dy + 24α(1)σ₁(m)s^{−1}] + 24β(1)σ₁(m) + 48α(1)[σ′₁(m) − σ₁(m)(log 2m + 1/2 + ζ′/ζ(2))], where σ₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d, σ′₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d log d. (Proof: subtract Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)}, which is orthogonal to cusp forms and has expansion A(N₁) log y + B(N₁) + O(y^{−1} log y) at ξ, then apply the case A = B = 0.)

Subtract Σ_M(α(M)F(Mz)+β(M)E(Mz)), which is cusp-orthogonal.

nodes.title: Eisenstein Mellin asymptotics
nodes.statement: Write E(z) = Σ_m e(m,y)e^{2πimz}, F(z) = Σ_m f(m,y)e^{2πimz}. For m > 0: e(m,y) = −24σ₁(m), and as s → 0 (Re s > 0): ∫₀^∞ e(m,y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = −(6/(πm))σ₁(m) + o(1); ∫₀^∞ f(m,y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = ∂/∂t[−2π^{3/2+t}m^{−1/2−t}Γ(s+t+1)Γ(s−t)σ_{1+2t}(m)/((4πm)^{s+1/2}Γ(2+t)Γ(s)ζ(2+2t))]_{t=0} = −24 Γ(s+1)/(4πm)^{s+1} · [2σ′₁(m) + σ₁(m)(log(π/m) + γ − 1 − 2ζ′/ζ(2) + 1/s)] = −(6/(πm))σ₁(m)s^{−1} − (12/(πm))σ′₁(m) + (12/(πm))σ₁(m)(log 2m + ½ + ζ′/ζ(2)) + o(1), γ = Euler's constant. Put a′ = (M/(M,N₁))a, c′ = c/(M,N₁) ((a′,c′) = 1), complete to α′ = (a′ b′; c′ d′) ∈ SL₂(ℤ), and relate z, z′ by c′z′ + d′ = ((M,N₁)/M)(cz+d); then (a′z′+b′)/(c′z′+d′) = M(az+b)/(cz+d), y′ = ((M,N₁)²/M)y, and E_{2,s}(Mz)|₂α = ((M,N₁)^{2+2s}/M^{2+s}) y^s + O(y^{−1−s}); hence E(Mz)|₂α = (M,N₁)²/M² + O(1/y), F(Mz)|₂α = ((M,N₁)²/M²)(log y + log((M,N₁)²/M)) + O(y^{−1} log y). nodes.title: Boundary Eisenstein orthogonality
nodes.statement: Let N ≥ 1 and M | N, and let E(z) = E_{2,s}(z)|_{s=0}, F(z) = ∂_sE_{2,s}(z)|_{s=0} as in the proof of (6.2) (the referenced classical source result 264). Consequently Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)} has the same Petersson products with cusp forms as 0, and Φ̃ and Φ̃* = Φ̃ − Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)} have the same holomorphic projection.

nodes.title: Cusp constant matrix inverse
nodes.statement: Let C_N = (C_N(N₁, M))_{N₁, M | N}, C_N(N₁, M) = (M, N₁)²/M² (a σ₀(N) × σ₀(N) matrix). The entries are multiplicative, C_{∏p^{ν_p}}(∏p^{λ_p}, ∏p^{μ_p}) = ∏ C_{p^{ν_p}}(p^{λ_p}, p^{μ_p}), so C_N is the Kronecker product of the C_{p^ν} (N = ∏ p^ν). For N = p^ν, C_{p^ν}(p^λ, p^μ) = p^{2 min(λ,μ) − 2μ} (rows λ = 0..ν: (1, p^{−2}, …, p^{−2ν}), (1, 1, p^{−2}, …, p^{−2ν+2}), …, (1, …, 1)), and (6.6) C_{p^ν}^{−1} = (p² − 1)^{−1} × the tridiagonal matrix with diagonal (p², p²+1, …, p²+1, p²), superdiagonal −1, subdiagonal −p². In particular C_N is invertible and (6.3)-(6.4) have a unique solution. The displayed tridiagonal inverse is for ν≥1; for ν=0 use the 1×1 matrix (1).

Multiply the prime-power matrix by the displayed tridiagonal inverse; both corner rows must be checked. The ν=0 matrix is (1), handled separately.

nodes.title: Half-weight Waldspurger value
nodes.statement: Let φ(z)=2√y Σ_(n≠0) a(n)K_(ir)(2π|n|y)e(nx) be a nonzero even level-one Hecke–Maass eigenform, a(1)=1. Choose the associated weight-1/2 Kohnen-plus eigenline at parameter r/2 and its vector F(z)=Σ b(n)W_(sgn(n)/4,ir/2)(4π|n|y)e(nx), normalized by (F,F)=1 under the DIT Petersson convention. For a nonzero fundamental discriminant d, 12π|d||b(d)|²=(φ,φ)⁻¹Γ(1/2+ir/2−sgn(d)/4)Γ(1/2−ir/2−sgn(d)/4)L(1/2,φ⊗χ_d). The phase of F is free and both sides are phase-invariant. The half-weight form has the specified Whittaker and Petersson normalization, including the plus condition at 2
proofSteps: Import the Hecke-equivariant Kohnen-plus/GL₂ eigenline correspondence, including the operator at 2 and the eigenvalue parameter r/2.
Apply the local/global Baruch–Mao central-value identity.
Compare its Whittaker coefficient and Petersson conventions with DIT Theorem4 and (5.17), retaining 12π and both signed gamma factors.
Pass to the unit half-weight vector; its arbitrary phase disappears in |b(d)|².

nodes.title: CM tensor stabilizer height
nodes.statement: Let x be a chosen integral Γ₀(N)-diagram over the complete characteristic-zero DVR W whose section is in the smooth locus of the coarse model. Let ω_x be a nonzero rational cotangent vector, u_x=#Aut_F(x)/2, and θ a nonzero global differential tensor of weight k with order r_x at x; assume r_x+k≠0. For x=(ℂ/𝔞→ℂ/𝔞𝔫⁻¹), with 𝔞𝔫⁻¹ integral, it identifies the corresponding τ in 𝔥 by (1.4) Aτ²+Bτ+C=0, A>0, B²−4AC=D, A≡0(mod N), B≡β(mod 2N). It gives (1.5) 𝔞=ℤ·A+ℤ(B+√D)/2, 𝔞𝔫⁻¹=ℤ·AN⁻¹+ℤ(B+√D)/2, N_{K/ℚ}(𝔞)=A.
sourceIssues.correction: With √D = i√|D| (the branch §3 uses: "τ_i∈A_i⁻¹𝔞̄_i=𝔞_i⁻¹" in (3.7) and "cτ₁+d=(β−α)/(τ₂−τ̄₂)=(A₂/√D)(β−α)" on p. 245) the root τ ∈ 𝔥 represents (ℂ/𝔞̄ → ℂ/𝔞̄𝔫̄⁻¹) = c(x), i.e. the pair (𝒜⁻¹, 𝔫̄); x itself is −τ̄ = (B+√D)/(2A). Consistent fixes: read (β+√D)/2, (B+√D)/2 as (−β+√D)/2, (−B+√D)/2 in (1.3), (1.5) (then (3.7) reads τ_i ∈ 𝔞̄_i⁻¹), or keep (1.3)–(1.5) and read τ_{𝒜,𝔫} in §3 as the Heegner point (𝒜⁻¹, 𝔫̄), on which σ_𝒜 acts by 𝒜₁ ↦ 𝒜₁𝒜.
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: §1 dictionary (p. 234): z = ω₁/ω₂ for an oriented basis ⟨ω₁, ω₂⟩ of L with ⟨ω₁, ω₂/N⟩ a basis of L′. For L = 𝔞 = ℤA + ℤ(B+√D)/2 and L′ = 𝔞𝔫⁻¹ = ℤA/N + ℤ(B+√D)/2 this is ω₁ = (B+√D)/2, ω₂ = A (Im(ω₁ω̄₂) = A√|D|/2 > 0), z = (B+√D)/(2A), a root of Az² − Bz + C with B-invariant −β (mod 2N), which differs from β for N > 1 because (β, N) = 1; equivalently Aτ = (−B+√D)/2 ∈ 𝔞̄, so ⟨τ, 1⟩ ~ 𝔞̄ (checked numerically for D = −7, −23: Aτ ∈ 𝔞̄, Aτ ∉ 𝔞). The paper states that 'this invariant corresponds to the choice of 𝔫 as in (1.3)'; under the dictionary it corresponds to 𝔫̄. Reach: every result of Chapter II depends on the classes only through r_𝒜, r_𝔅, δ(n) and the genera {𝒜}, {𝔅𝔫}, all invariant under (𝒜, 𝔅, 𝔫) ↦ (𝒜⁻¹, 𝔅⁻¹, 𝔫̄); (3.14)/(3.17) were verified numerically in the τ-labelling. Chunks reading §4–§5 and Chapter V (individual terms (3.1), χ-components) should keep the labelling in mind: it swaps χ and χ⁻¹, which the paper's final formulas pair symmetrically.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter II, §3, (3.11) Proposition and the converse step on p. 245, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: Proposition (3.11) takes classes 𝒜₁, 𝒜₂ of K, primitive 𝔫 of norm N, and integral 𝔞_i in 𝒜_i (i=1, 2), with 𝔫|𝔞_i, N(𝔞_i)=A_i. For m∈ℕ, r_{𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹}(m)=0, it gives ρ^m(n) = #{(α, β)∈(𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞̄₂⁻¹×𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞₂⁻¹𝔫)/{±1} | N(α)=(Nn+m|D|)/(A₁A₂), N(β)=Nn/(A₁A₂), A₁A₂α≡A₁A₂β(mod 𝔡)}. On p. 245 it claims (3.7), (3.10) put their right sides respectively in 𝔫𝔞₁⁻¹=Nℤτ₁+ℤ and 𝔞₁⁻¹=ℤτ₁+ℤ.
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis that 𝔞₁, 𝔞₂ are prime to D (possible in every class, keeping 𝔫 | 𝔞_i), or replace (3.10) by the exact conditions (A₂/√D)(β − α) ∈ 𝔫𝔞₁⁻¹ and (A₂/√D)(τ̄₂β − τ₂α) ∈ 𝔞₁⁻¹.
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: The converse divides by √D; at a ramified 𝔭 | 𝔞₁ (or 𝔞₂) the numbers A₁A₂α, A₁A₂β lie in 𝔭 automatically, so (3.10) carries no information there. Counterexample (SCR/t_rho.py, t_rho2.py; recomputed independently by the reviewer): D = −7, N = 2, β = 1, m = 3 (3 inert, h = 1), τ₂ from [2, 1, 1], 𝔞₁ = ℤ14 + ℤ(21+√−7)/2 from [14, 21, 8] (N(𝔞₁) = 14, 𝔞₁ ⊂ (√−7)): the true γ-counts are ρ(1), ρ(2), ρ(4), ρ(8) = 2, 2, 6, 8 while the (α, β)-set of (3.11) has 4, 4, 12, 16 elements (every n with 7 ∤ n doubles; n = 14, 28 agree); with 𝔞₁ from [2, 1, 1] (prime to 7) the two counts agree for all n ≤ 29. The p. 246 argument for (3.13) ('exactly half of the pairs') also presupposes 𝔞ᵢ prime to D. Reach: Proposition (3.11) is false in its stated generality; nothing downstream is affected, because (3.12)–(3.17) are statements about classes and follow with representatives prime to D (verified numerically).

III (8.3) (p. 263, N = 1): from ω^{⊗6} = Δ(dq/q)^{⊗6} and q dj/dq = −E₆j/E₄ one gets ω = dj/(j^{2/3}(j − 1728)^{1/2}) up to a root of unity; at j = 1728 (u = 2) the corrected normalization gives ∂/∂t = 2⁶·3⁴ ∂/∂j and the printed one 2⁸·3⁴ ∂/∂j, and at j = 0 (u = 3) the corrected one gives |2⁹·3^{3/2}| and the printed one |2⁹·3^{9/2}|; (8.3), read on a full-resolution IIIF crop of image 00000269, prints 'α ≡ j(x)^{2/3}(j(x) − 1728)^{1/2} (mod μ₀), j(x) ≠ 0, 1728; ≡ 2⁶ · 3⁴, j(x) = 1728; ≡ 2⁹ · 3^{3/2}, j(x) = 0' — exactly the three values computed with the corrected normalization (the generic value j^{2/3}(j − 1728)^{1/2} is the same for both, since u = 1 there). sourceIssues.locator: Chapter III, §1, definition of 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} (p. 254) and the description of the cusps (p. 255), Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source defines 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} as the algebraic stack of cyclic degree N isogenies (1.1) φ: E → E′ between generalized elliptic curves over S, requiring A = ker φ to meet all irreducible components in every geometric fibre. It takes X as the coarse moduli scheme of 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)}. It describes Cusp(d) using Néron polygon diagrams with A = ker φ isomorphic to μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ.
sourceIssues.correction: 'A = ker φ is isomorphic to μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ' holds only when gcd(d, N/d) = 1. In general, at the cuspidal points of Cusp(d) the kernel A is a cyclic group scheme of order N that is an extension of dℤ/Nℤ ≅ ℤ/(N/d)ℤ by μ_d, and it is non-split when f = gcd(d, N/d) > 1 (on a Néron polygon, e.g. ⟨(ζ_N, 1)⟩ ⊂ G_m × ℤ/(N/d)ℤ). The coarse moduli scheme X of (1.1)–(1.2) is still the Deligne–Rapoport and Katz–Mazur model of X₀(N) (Česnavičius 2017, §1.1), so the model itself needs no change; but for N not squarefree the stack 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} of (1.1)–(1.2) differs from the Deligne–Rapoport stack at these cusps, and Česnavičius' refined Γ₀(N)-structures give the correct moduli description there.
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: (i) Check: Cusp(d) ≅ Spec ℤ[μ_f] is flat over ℤ, so its geometric points include characteristic-0 points; there μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ ≅ ℤ/d × ℤ/(N/d) is not cyclic when f = gcd(d, N/d) > 1, contradicting the cyclicity condition (1.2) that defines 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)}. On a Néron polygon a cyclic A of order N meeting every component is e.g. ⟨(ζ_N, 1)⟩ ⊂ G_m × ℤ/(N/d), a non-split extension. (ii) Česnavičius, 'A modular description of X₀(n)', Algebra & Number Theory 11 (2017) (arXiv:1511.07475), abstract: 'when a positive integer n is not squarefree, even over ℂ the moduli stack that parametrizes generalized elliptic curves equipped with an ample cyclic subgroup of order n does not agree at the cusps with the Γ₀(n)-level modular stack'. The stack of (1.1)–(1.2) is exactly that naive stack. Katz–Mazur [21] treat [Γ₀(N)] only for elliptic curves and compactify by normalization, so the generalized-elliptic-curve description is not in the cited sources for non-squarefree N. Wording re-checked on imgHR/p254.jpg and p255.jpg ('A = ker φ is isomorphic to μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ'). (Also recorded by an earlier worker: Česnavičius 2017 (for the moduli description at the cusps); the inconsistency with the stated group structure μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ is new. The atlas stage ModularCurvesPartII:R13.2 already routes around it ('Follow Česnavičius' refined description when the naive cyclic-subgroup formulation fails')..)
sourceIssues.known: new (for this sentence). The underlying failure of the naive cyclic-subgroup stack at the cusps for non-squarefree N is in print: K. Conrad, Arithmetic moduli of generalized elliptic curves, 2007); none of these comments on this sentence of the paper.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter III, §2, paragraph after (2.1), p. 256, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source uses algebraic closedness of k to claim that Hom_S(y, x) does not depend on which diagrams represent x and y.
sourceIssues.correction: True for S = W (a complete DVR of characteristic 0 with algebraically closed residue field: two W-diagrams inducing the same W-point are isomorphic, Conrad Theorem 2.6) and hence for the reductions to W/πⁿ of fixed W-diagrams, which is the only way §§4–9 use it; false for general complete local S (e.g. artinian S) at points with Aut_k ≠ ⟨±1⟩, where Hom_S must be defined for chosen diagrams.
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: Counterexample: p ≥ 5, N = 2, E: y² = x³ − x over 𝔽̄_p with p ≡ 1 (mod 4) (ordinary, j = 1728), A = ⟨(0,0)⟩, which is stable under [i]: (x, y) ↦ (−x, iy); so Aut_k(x₀) = μ₄. The universal deformation ring is W[[T]] with Aut/±1 = ℤ/2 acting faithfully (Conrad p. 12), linearizably T ↦ −T, so the complete local ring of X is W[[T²]] (Conrad Lemma 4.2). Over S = k[ε]/(ε²) the deformations T ↦ 0 (constant) and T ↦ ε both give T² ↦ 0, i.e. the same S-point of X, but they are not isomorphic: the constant one has Aut_S = μ₄, while [i] carries T ↦ ε to T ↦ −ε ≠ ε, so the other has Aut_S = ±1. Hence Card Hom_S(y, y)_{deg 1} is 4 or 2 depending on the representing diagram. Wording re-checked on imgHR/p256.jpg. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: new (Conrad 2004 restricts to W-diagrams: Theorem 2.6 and Lemma 4.2, conrad.txt pp. 6 and 11).)

sourceIssues.correction: ∂/∂t spans (N)^{−u} T_x X when v|n̄, i.e. ∂/∂t = N^{−u}·(generator). Equivalently ω_x is N^u times a generator of the cotangent line. With the corrected (8.1) (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E16) this gives (x·x) = −u·ord_v(N), and hence Proposition (8.6) as printed.
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: When v|n̄ the kernel of φ is étale at p, and x lies on the fibral component through the cusp 0 = Cusp(1) (Prop. 3.1). Near that cusp the integral parameter is q′ = e^{2πiτ′}, τ′ = −1/(Nτ), attached to the Tate curve Tate(q′^N) with subgroup ⟨q′⟩. From η(−1/(Nτ′)) = (Nτ′/i)^{1/2}η(Nτ′) one gets ω = 2πiη⁴(τ)dτ = −N·η⁴(q′^N)dq′/q′. So ω vanishes to order ord_p(N) along that component: it is N times a generator. Equivalently, on the étale-kernel component the forgetful map (E→E′) ↦ E is inseparable (Frobenius), so ω = π_1^*ω_1 ≡ 0 mod p. The dual vector ∂/∂t is therefore N^{−1}·(generator) when u = 1; for u > 1 the normalisation ω = (g^{1/u}+…)dg/g raises this to N^{−u}. Conrad's Lemma 10.1 independently gives ord_{v,x}(Δ) = 6u·ord_v(N) in exactly this étale case, i.e. Δ(dq/q)^{⊗6} = ω^6 is N^6 times a generator. The printed (8.6) value −u r_𝒜(m) ord_p(N) is correct (Conrad Thm 10.4). It is obtained from the printed '(N)^u' only together with the literal (inverted) wording of (8.1), so the two misstatements cancel. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: new (the underlying fact is Conrad 2004, Lemma 10.1 and Theorem 10.4, which do not comment on GZ's sentence).)

sourceIssues.correction: For S (with the congruence α ≡ β) to be an order one needs −pq ≡ 1 (mod l) for every prime l|D, i.e. −pq ≡ 1 (mod D); in the ramified case one needs −q ≡ 1 (mod D/p). Both can be imposed alongside GZ's conditions and still met by Dirichlet's theorem. Alternatively use the congruence α ≡ Xβ with N(X) ≡ −pq (mod D) (Mann's S_X, (A.5)/(A.6)). The sign bookkeeping α ≡ ±β in (9.3), (9.8) and in the proof of (9.7) then applies verbatim.
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: Let l|D and let 𝔣 be the prime over l. Take α = β ∈ 𝔡^{-1} with a simple pole at 𝔣; then α+βj ∈ S. Its reduced norm is N(α)+pqN(β) = (1+pq)N(β), and ord_l N(β) = −1. So the norm is l-integral only if l | 1+pq. GZ's condition says only that −pq is a square mod l (e.g. −pq ≡ 4 mod l is allowed), so S can contain elements of non-integral reduced norm, and is then not an order. The proof of (9.7) also uses −pq ≡ 1 mod l when it concludes that integrality of mN𝔞 = Nα + pqNβ forces α ≡ ±β mod O_𝔣. With −pq ≡ X² one gets only α ≡ ±Xβ. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: Mann, appendix to Conrad 2004, p. 57 ('certainly one does not get an order in (A.5) using X = 1 unless −pq ≡ 1 mod D'; ramified case: 'take X = 1 (as in [GZ]) by also requiring −q ≡ 1 mod D/p'), and Remark A.7.)
sourceIssues.known: W. R. Mann, Appendix A to B. Conrad, Gross–Zagier revisited, in Heegner points and Rankin L-series, MSRI Publ. 49 (2004): in the discussion of (A.5) and (A.6) he writes 'If we had also required −pq ≡ 1 mod D, then we could have taken X = 1 (see Remark A.7). sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: Part a) assumes (4.2) explicitly; part b) does not, but its proof (p. 287: ‘this was shown at the beginning of the section to be zero under the hypotheses of (b)’) uses Σ_{d|n} ε_𝒜(n,d) = 0, which follows from (4.3) only for n satisfying (4.2); Remark 2 uses the same vanishing. Machine check over D ∈ {−15, −35, −39, −55, −195, −231}, N ≤ 41, all classes, n ≤ 120: with (4.2) all 6 237 cases agree; without it the formula fails in hundreds of cases for every D with more than one genus (never for D = −7, one genus). sourceIssues.locator: Chapter II, §2, p. 241, last paragraph (the sentence leading to the display before (2.23)), Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source bases the following conclusion on the claim that T_m fixes every cusp.
sourceIssues.correction: Since T_m((∞)) = σ₁(m)(∞) and T_m((0)) = σ₁(m)(0) for (m, N) = 1, we have … (the displayed identity is unchanged). T_m does not fix the other cusps in general: it fixes every cusp for all m prime to N if and only if every f_d = (d, N/d) is at most 2, i.e. if and only if N is divisible neither by 9, nor by 16, nor by p² for a prime p ≥ 5.
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: For a cusp u/v in lowest terms with d = (v, N) and f = f_d, the Γ₀(N)-class is determined by d and the label (v/d)·u mod f (the corrected label of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E1). For a coset representative (a b; 0 δ) of Γ₀(N)\{γ ∈ R_N : det γ = m}, aδ = m, the image (au + bv)/(δv) reduces by g = gcd(au + bv, δv), which is prime to N; the new denominator has the same d, and since f | v the label becomes (m/g²)·(v/d)·u mod f. Taking the representative (m 0; 0 1) with m prime to v gives the factor m, which is not 1 mod f for suitable m once f ≥ 3. Brute force (plain Python: Γ₀(N)-equivalence tested through γ = M′T^kM⁻¹, all k mod N and both signs): N = 9, m = 2: T₂(1/3) = 3·(2/3), and 1/3, 2/3 are inequivalent cusps of Γ₀(9); N = 25, m = 2: T₂(1/5) = 2·(2/5) + (3/5); N = 16, m = 3: T₃ swaps 1/4 and 3/4; N = 6, 8, 12: every cusp fixed. The cusps ∞ and 0 have f = 1 and are always fixed, and they are the only cusps the argument uses (c = (x) − (∞), T_m((x′) − (0))), so nothing downstream changes.

sourceIssues.printed: Proposition (1.4) claims regularity of X over ℤ away from supersingular x in characteristics p|N with Aut_k(x) ≠ ⟨±1⟩. The proof of (3.3) says that resolving quotient singularities at the supersingular points of X over ℤ produces a regular model X^reg.

The resolution X^reg in (3.3) must also resolve the ordinary ones (points with j = 1728 or j = 0 on 𝓕_{a,b}, a, b ≥ 1, possible when p² | N).
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: Take N = p², p ≡ 1 (mod 4), and x = (E, A) with E ordinary over k = 𝔽̄_p, j(E) = 1728, on the component 𝓕_{1,1} (A ≅ μ_p × ℤ/p, multiplicity φ(p) = p − 1). The connected and étale parts of A are characteristic, so [i] preserves A and Aut_k(x) = μ₄ ≠ ⟨±1⟩, although x is ordinary. Over the Serre–Tate deformation ring W[[T]], q = 1 + T, the cyclic subgroups of order p² reducing to A are ⟨(x, p)⟩ with x^p = qζ, ζ a primitive p-th root of unity, so the complete local ring of the (regular) stack at x is W[ζ_p][[T]]. The automorphism [i] acts on E[p^∞] by u on the connected part and ū = −u on the étale part (u² = −1 in ℤ_p), hence by q ↦ q^{−1} (T ↦ −T + O(T²)) and ζ ↦ ζ^{−1}: it acts as −1 on the cotangent space ⟨ζ − 1, T⟩, which is not generated by pseudo-reflections. By Serre's criterion (2 invertible) the complete local ring of X at x, the invariant ring, is not regular; explicitly it is W⁺[[X, Y]]/(Y² − ϖ₊X) with X = T′², Y = (ζ − ζ^{−1})T′, T′ = (q − q^{−1})/2, W⁺ = W[ζ + ζ^{−1}], ϖ₊ = (ζ − ζ^{−1})², of embedding dimension 3. The same happens for j = 0, p ≡ 1 (mod 3), where the automorphism of order 3 acts by a primitive cube root of unity on both cotangent directions.

sourceIssues.correction: ω′ = ω/√D, with ω transported to E′ by the K-isomorphism E′ ≅ E, (x, y) ↦ (x, √D·y), and √D = ±i√|D|.
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: For E′: Dy² = x³ + ax + b and φ(x, y) = (x, √D·y), φ*(dx/2y) = (dx/2y)/√D, and a Galois element moving √D changes the sign of both φ*ω and √D, so φ*ω/√D is ℚ-rational while φ*ω/√|D| = ±i·φ*ω/√D is not. Up to sign φ*ω/√D is the Néron differential of E′ (unramified at p ∤ 2D and at 2 since D ≡ 1 mod 4; at odd p | D compare the I₀*-minimal model, v_p(Δ) = 6, with the good model over ℤ_p[√D]). The identity ‖ω‖²/|D|^{1/2} = [E(ℝ):E(ℝ)⁰]·Ω·Ω′ on the same page holds for this Ω′ (checked with mpmath for E = 11a1, D = −7, −19, −43; for D = −7, Ω′ = 0.183794), whereas the periods of ω/√|D| are those of E scaled by 1/√7 (real period 0.079953) and the identity would fail.

sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 8.7(2) asserts n_{φ_v}(y,u) = φ_v(y,u)·½v(q(y)) for every non-archimedean place v of F and every (y,u) ∈ E_v^×× F_v^×. Its proof on p. 619 says that the analogous computation for v ∈ S2 yields 0 everywhere.

Then n_{φ_v}(y,u) = −(1+N_v+N_v²)^{-1}ψ2(y,u) on E_v^××F_v^×, which is not 0; for example n_{φ_v}(1,1) = −1/(1+N_v+N_v²). The printed value is φ_v(1,1)·0 = 0. The lemma is correct for v ∉ S2. Prop. 9.2(2) and Theorem 9.1 still hold, because Lemma 7.6(2) fails at S2 by exactly the compensating amount: c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = −(2log N_v/(1+N_v+N_v²))ψ2(y,u). Hence d_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = 2n_{φ_v}log N_v − c_{φ_v} + log|uq(y)|_vφ_v = 0 = −log|d_vq(𝗃_v)|_vφ_v(y,u). The proof of Prop. 9.2(2) at S2 must use both corrected values.
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: Use the formula of Prop. 8.5 with U_v = GL2(O_{F_v}) (Assumption 7.1), r = 0, so m_ν̄1(n(b)) = 1/(N_v^{−v(b)−1}(N_v−1)) and each shell v(b) = −i contributes 1. For b ∉ O, y·n(b) ∉ GL2(O), so the ψ1 part is 0. For y = diag(a,d), y·n(b) ∈ ϖ^{-1}(O_{𝔹_v})_2 if and only if v(a),v(d) ≥ −1, v(a)+v(d) = 0 and v(ab) ≥ −1. So the upper sum is 1+v(a), the lower 1+v(d), and n_{ψ2} = ½(2+v(ad)) = 1 on supp ψ2|_E. A brute-force enumeration for p = 2 and p = 3 (y = 1, diag(p^{-1},p), diag(p,p^{-1})) gives n = −1/7 and −1/13, against 0 printed. Checked on the page image. Checker 3 found the same error independently (as an out-of-range entry); merge the two. Independent second check (checker 3): Apply Prop. 8.5 with U_v = GL2(O_v) (r = 0): m_{ν1}(n(b)) = 1/(N^{−v(b)−1}(N−1)), so each shell v(b) = −i ≤ −1 contributes 1. ψ1(y n(b)) = 0 for b ∉ O. sourceIssues.locator: Section A.1, p. 102 (the condition equivalent to admissibility of a Green function)
sourceIssues.printed: The source identifies the condition with the current equation (i/pi) ddbar g_D = dmu_Ar - delta_D on C.
sourceIssues.correction: (i/pi) ddbar g_D = deg(D) dmu_Ar - delta_D
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: The identity fails on total mass for every divisor of degree other than 1. The left side is exact, so it integrates to 0 over the compact surface C. The paper's own normalization makes mu_Ar a probability measure: dmu_Ar = (i/2g) sum_j alpha_j wedge alpha_j-bar for an orthonormal basis of the pairing <alpha,beta> = (i/2) integral alpha wedge beta-bar, so its total mass is (1/g) times g, namely 1; and delta_D has total mass deg(D). As printed the right side integrates to 1 - deg(D). The factor is also forced by the two neighbouring definitions: admissibility of a metric is defined three lines earlier as c_1(L,||.||) = deg(L) dmu_Ar, and Poincare-Lelong for ||1|| = exp(-g_D), the paper's own convention, gives c_1(O(D),||.||) = (i/pi) ddbar g_D + delta_D, so substituting admissibility produces the deg(D). The non-archimedean twin, Proposition A.2 on p. 108, correctly carries deg(L). Nothing downstream breaks, because every subsequent use is for a divisor D = x_0 of degree 1.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition A.5, p. 118, and one step of the existence proof of Theorem A.1, p. 113
sourceIssues.printed: Appendix A assumes genus g > 0 throughout; this hypothesis accompanies Theorem A.1, Proposition A.2, Theorem A.3, and Proposition A.5.
sourceIssues.correction: two steps need g > 1 and are unproved at g = 1
sourceIssues.reason: Prior reviewed extraction check: Two steps silently require 2g - 2 to be nonzero. First, the proof of Proposition A.5 computes c_1(omega_{C/K}, ||.||_a) = i_*((2g-2) mu) and then appeals to the defining equation of dmu_a, which for L = omega reads c_1(omega, ||.||_a) = deg(omega) dmu_a = (2g-2) dmu_a; at g = 1 this is 0 = 0 and determines nothing. The asserted formula nevertheless appears to be true at g = 1 - good reduction gives the single vertex measure, and a Tate curve with an n-cycle graph gives uniform probability measure on the edges - so this is a gap rather than a false statement, and the fix is to run the argument with a degree-1 line bundle instead of omega. Second, the existence half of Theorem A.1 concludes on p. 113 that 'The constancy of this integral with L = omega_{C/K} is exactly what we need for (2) of Theorem A.1'; but property (2) as stated integrates against c_1(O(x), ||.||_x), and the omega-version is equivalent to it only under the paper's own proviso on p. 105, 'Note that if g > 1, the first two properties are equivalent to the following'. That the author was tracking the g-dependence is clear from the neighbouring uniqueness proof, which inserts '(for g > 0)' exactly where it is needed; these two steps do not survive g = 1.

Canonical Jacobian height for 2Θ, positivity modulo torsion and complex Hermitian extension; specialize the general ample canonical-height machine, without redefining it in GZ.
Ideal-class CM points and Hecke correspondences on X₀(N), field-of-definition and Artin reciprocity with the source ideal-inverse convention.
The BSD rank-one prediction over K and its exact index, regulator, torsion and Tamagawa convention; this is a consumer conjecture, not an arithmetic-height theorem proved here.

Hom/End of chosen cyclic N-isogeny diagrams over complete local and Artinian bases; degree equality, finite positive-degree fibres, free sign action and faithful stabilizer action. Do not assert choice-independent Hom for arbitrary coarse Artinian points with extra automorphisms.
Quasicanonical CM lifting/isogeny intersection calculation over W, including the prime-to-p degree decomposition and the valuation normalization used in the classical Hom sum.
Exact negative-norm coset/congruence lifting count in the quaternionic CM deformation order, including ramified and dyadic ranges.
Canonical ordinary CM lifting and fullness of reduction on CM Hom/End; prove the classical new-Hom vanishing at split places.
Quaternionic norm-positive/anti-linear decomposition compatible with the embedded K and reduced norm, including norm/degree ratio for connecting Hom ideals.
Gross canonical-lift endomorphism filtration over W/π^n, in the source uniformizer convention; distinguish inert and ramified lengths and state the dyadic exceptions.
Connecting ideals between optimal CM Eichler orders and their orientation identity; provide both 𝔟R=S𝔟 and R𝔟=𝔟S conventions and the induced anti-linear coefficient ratio.
Scalar modular forms of weight 2k and polynomial growth at every cusp, trace of levels and Petersson integrability against cusp forms; import their actual classical realization.
Genus characters of the ideal class group, ordered fundamental discriminant factorizations, quadratic character evaluations and theta transformation under ramified ideals.
The norm representation and genus criterion with Nn+l≡0 mod D and l a norm from the specified class. This hypothesis is necessary for the divisor complement identities.
Regularized Petersson holomorphic projection in weight two with logarithmic cusp growth, Fourier Mellin finite parts, continuation bounds and orthogonality of boundary Eisenstein families.
The field-of-definition and complex conjugation of classical Heegner points and their modular images, in the source Artin/Fricke convention.
